Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: 9 in 10 Indians research festive purchases online, but 70% buy on impulse: Google study
Article Text:
9 in 10 Indians research festive purchases online, but 70% buy on impulse: Google study

What the study says

A Google-commissioned Ipsos consumer study has found that Indian festive shoppers are operating at two very different speeds. According to it, 9 in 10 consumers conduct extensive online research before buying—discovering new brands, comparing prices, and checking reviews. While 70% of festive purchases are decided in the moment, sparked by visual discovery and festive urgency.Roma Datta Chobey, Managing Director, Connected Consumer Commerce, Google India, said, “What stands out across India’s festive season is how deliberate research and spontaneous impulse coexist. Shoppers are taking richer, AI-guided journeys to evaluate trade-offs, yet they are equally ready to check out in hours when sparked by video and rapid delivery. With choices remaining fluid right up to the final mile, Google and YouTube sit at the heart of this behavior. Winning this season means meeting consumers at both speeds: building deep relevance during deliberation and moving fast to capture immediate demand—an agility unlocked by our Gemini-powered solutions. ”Some of the findings are:● AI is becoming an essential festive shopping companion, with consumers consulting chatbots an average of 7.5 times, especially when evaluating categories like electronics, appliances, home decor, and personal care.This creates a more curious consumer for whom conversations act as a springboard: across shopping journeys more broadly, AI users explore 2.8x more touchpoints online as they seek deeper context.● 51% of festive shoppers credit AI with helping them make choices. This expertise flexes across different needs: shoppers lean on AI for highly specific, tailored answers in personal care and beauty, while using it to demystify complex specs, refine criteria, and evaluate trade-offs in categories like home appliances and consumer electronics. Aided with knowledge they never previously considered, buyers navigate choices with authority—a shift echoed beyond festive season, where 87% of users report making decisions with higher confidence using AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search.● Alongside planned research, festive shopping carries a high-momentum spontaneous track where immediate appeal drives the cart. Google and YouTube directly influence 54% of these unplanned purchases, the study claimed adding it is driven primarily by festive urgency, compelling offers, and the instant pull of discovering an appealing product in the moment.● Visual inspiration and creators turn ideas into instant buys: Visual cues are the primary catalyst for quick action. As celebrations approach, styling searches surge and shoppers act directly on what catches their eye: 53% use visual tools like Google Lens to discover or compare products, while creators and short-form video close the decision loop. 73% of festive buyers turn to creators for inspiration, and 61% of those who made purchases within a couple of days or less without prior research used YouTube Shorts in their shopping journeys.●Delivery timing has become critical, with 90% of shoppers viewing sub-two-day delivery as non-negotiable and 81% choosing retailers based on speed. This demand for immediacy is already visible around key festivals this season: Google Trends recorded a sharp surge in searches for “same day delivery rakhi” a day before Rakshabandhan this year.Across every entry point, shoppers naturally integrate the platforms into their journey: among consumers using AI chatbots, 94% concurrently turn to Google Search and 87% to YouTube, while 7 in 10 shoppers who spot products on social media turn to Google Search to evaluate them further.Because consumers continuously explore and cross-check across channels, festive choices remain fluid right up to checkout. 8 in 10 shoppers report being open to trying new retailers — an intent that actively plays out on Google, where 51% of shoppers using Google Search and/or YouTube discover new products along their journey.
Article Summary: 9 in 10 Indians research festive purchases online, but 70% buy on impulse. Google and YouTube directly influence 54% of these unplanned purchases. Google Trends recorded a sharp surge in searches for ‘same day delivery rakhi’ a day before Rakshabandhan.

Article Title: Religious, spiritual & astrology apps see nearly 30cr downloads in Jan-Sept
Article Text: NEW DELHI: From listening to bhajans and reading the Bible to finding the direction of Mecca or discovering what the stars have in store, Indians are increasingly turning to smartphones for matters of faith and fortune. Religious, spiritual and astrology apps recorded nearly 30 crore downloads in the first nine months of 2026, emerging as fast-growing segments of India's app economy.According to data shared exclusively with TOI by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, astrology apps registered 15 crore downloads between Jan and Sept, a 75% jump over last year. Religious and spiritual apps clocked 14.6 crore downloads, up 47%. Together, the categories surpassed their combined 24.8 crore downloads in the whole of 2025 and touched nearly 30 crore downloads.The digital devotion wave is cutting across religions. Sanatan Status Bhajan Mantra topped the religious and spiritual category by average monthly active users, followed by YouVersion Bible App, which offers Bible reading and audio content, and WeMuslim, which provides prayer timings and Qibla direction.Sri Mandir, offering online pujas and devotional services, ranked fourth, while Muslim Pro, which provides Quran reading and prayer-related features, completed the top five.The diversity is also reflected in user growth. Sanatan Status Bhajan Mantra saw its average monthly active users jump 109% year-on-year, while YouVersion recorded 24% growth and WeMuslim 39%. Muslim Pro grew 5%, although Sri Mandir witnessed a 20% decline. "India's strong cultural affinity with religion and astrology, combined with its mobile-first consumer base, creates a favourable environment for growth in these categories," said Eve Chen, insights analyst, Sensor Tower.Indians are spending more time on these apps. Average daily usage of religious and spiritual apps rose from 5.8 minutes in the first quarter of 2022 to 8.2 minutes in corresponding quarter of 2026, a rise of over 40%. For astrology apps, engagement climbed more than 50%, from 3.5 to 5.3 minutes.Astrology is witnessing an AI-powered shift. Astrotalk led with 3 crore downloads, followed by AstroSage Kundli: AI Astrology at 2.5 crore, up 172%. Newer entrant Tarot99 recorded 1.1 crore downloads, while AstroLokal's downloads surged 1,062% to nearly 75 lakh.
Article Summary: Religious, spiritual and astrology apps recorded nearly 30 crore downloads in the first nine months of 2026. Astrology apps registered 15 crore downloads between Jan and Sept, a 75% jump over last year. Sanatan Status Bhajan Mantra topped the religious and spiritual category by average monthly active users.

Article Title: San Francisco software engineer called ‘horrible father’ after he jokes about using AI to read bedtime stories to his newborn
Article Text:
Representative image

Quick backlash across social media

Engineer pulls post, agrees to drop the topic

An attempt at tech humor by a Silicon Valley engineer has sparked widespread online backlash, after a software engineer joked about training an artificial intelligence (AI) voice model to read bedtime stories to his newborn child instead of doing it himself. Alvin Sng, a software engineer at the San Francisco-based AI research lab Factory, shared an exchange between himself and his wife on X (formerly Twitter) that quickly went viral for all the wrong reasons.According to Sng’s post (first reported by The New York Post), his wife asked him: “Can you read our baby a book?” When Sng suggested playing a standard audiobook instead, his wife pushed back, explaining that a pre-recorded tape would not be in his voice.“Me: I can train a voice model. Parenting hits different when you work in AI,” Sng recounted writing.The attempt to make light of automating infant care drew immediate criticism across the platform, with commentators labeling the attitude cold and disconnected. Direct replies criticised the premise bluntly, with one user stating, “Me: You are a horrible father.”Finance professional Andrew Lynch responded to the post calling it “absolute insanity,” adding, “These people’s brains are broken.”Aaron Fritschner, deputy chief of staff for Virginia Representative Don Beyer, characterized the exchange as “extremely bleak.”The exchange also tapped into broader cultural frustration regarding the direction of modern AI. Rather than taking over unpleasant physical labor, critics noted, automated systems are increasingly being directed at creative work and human bonding.“Truly can’t get over the fact that this technology came in and instead of using it to replace fixing toilets or folding clothes, people are using it to make movies and read to their kids,” one user remarked, adding, “This is maybe the saddest thing I’ve read on this site.”Other commentators argued that replacing personal parental presence with algorithmic clones could damage early child development. Influencer Michael Burns warned that relying on such methods risks raising children who are “unable to feel human love.”Following the mounting wave of criticism, Sng deleted the original post and issued a short follow-up note acknowledging the reaction:“Ok, enough jokes for a while. I’ll go back to reading bedtime stories for now,” he wrote on X the following day.
Article Summary: Alvin Sng, a software engineer at the San Francisco-based AI research lab Factory, shared an exchange between himself and his wife on X (formerly Twitter) that quickly went viral for all the wrong reasons. The attempt to make light of automating infant care drew immediate criticism across the platform.

Article Title: Anthropic launches free AI-powered security scanner for open-source software projects
Article Text:
How OSS Scanner from Anthropic works

Anthropic spent several weeks testing

How to join

AI giant Anthropic has introduced a free vulnerability-scanning service for open-source software projects, using its latest Claude models to identify security flaws and generate bug reports as the company expands its efforts to apply artificial intelligence to cybersecurity. The new service, called OSS Scanner, is an opt-in programme that offers periodic security scans to eligible open-source projects at no cost. Anthropic said the initiative draws on lessons from its vulnerability research efforts under Project Glasswing and is designed to help maintainers discover and fix software weaknesses before attackers can exploit them.According to Anthropic, language models have become significantly more capable at finding software vulnerabilities. The company said AI systems have improved from detecting fewer than 20% of vulnerabilities on a key academic benchmark early last year to finding more than 85% this year.OSS Scanner's output is fully model-generated, with no human review or triage. Anthropic said this allows faster and more frequent scans but means some reports may be incorrect or invalid. Each report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the vulnerability.Where possible it also traces when the bug was introduced, and it offers a candidate patch when one is available.Anthropic will keep sending human-verified reports through its existing coordinated vulnerability disclosure process, especially for projects that lack resources to triage reports themselves. OSS Scanner is an optional fast track for maintainers who want reports as soon as they are generated. It is separate from Claude Security, Anthropic's general-access code scanning and patching product for enterprises.Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of open-source projects. The first disclosures contained hundreds of bug reports, including several vulnerabilities that could be chained into unauthenticated remote code execution exploits.In one validation exercise, expert penetration testers who review Anthropic's disclosures checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects. Of these, 85 (88%) met the bar for the disclosure process. Of the other 12, 11 were real but duplicated known issues or other scan findings, and one was a false positive. Anthropic acknowledged that some maintainers have said severity ratings can be inflated, or that the scanner misunderstood a project's threat model.Maintainers who tested early versions were largely positive:* PostgreSQL: Noah Misch said several reports came with fixes the project could use nearly as they were, and that fast-track access let the team address new issues before a general-availability release.* OpenSSL Corporation: Anton Arapov said the reports, raw model output included, were as good as and sometimes better than those from people, especially when an exploit was attached.* wolfSSL: Todd Ouska said that of 74 reports, all but two were valid and five became CVEs.* HotCRP: Eddie Kohler praised the reports for their grasp of the project's complex permission model.Core maintainers of eligible projects can enroll by submitting a pull request to a GitHub repository Anthropic has set up. Eligibility follows criteria similar to OSS-Fuzz's, chiefly that a project has "critical impact on infrastructure and user security." Anthropic will decide case by case. Anthropic also pointed to two related programs: a Cyber Verification Program that gives qualifying security professionals advanced cyber capabilities with fewer blocking classifiers, and Claude for OSS, which offers free Claude Max 20x subscriptions to help fix vulnerabilities.
Article Summary: OSS Scanner is an opt-in programme that offers periodic security scans to eligible open-source projects at no cost. Anthropic said the initiative draws on lessons from its vulnerability research efforts under Project Glasswing. Each report includes a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the vulnerability.

Article Title: Microsoft makes major change to storage policy for Microsoft 365 Family, Premium and Pro plans; cuts OneDrive space across tiers: Here's how much storage subscribers will get now
Article Text:
Microsoft 365 Family storage drops from 6TB to 2TB

Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans drop from 6TB to a shared 2TB OneDrive pool

Existing Microsoft 365 subscribers get the new OneDrive limit after May 2, 2027

Copilot and AI features can now be shared with everyone on the plan

Microsoft is changing how OneDrive storage works on its Microsoft 365 Family, Premium and Pro subscriptions, and for most households that means less space. Instead of every member getting a dedicated 1TB, these plans are moving to a single storage pool that everyone on the subscription draws from.For a Family or Premium plan shared by the maximum six people, that pool will be 2TB. Today, the same group gets 6TB between them. That is a two-thirds cut in total cloud storage, on plans where OneDrive space has long been a big reason people subscribe, even if they rarely open Word or Excel.The Pro plan gets a larger shared pool of 5TB, according to Microsoft's updated support document. Files, photos and documents stay private to each member by default, so sharing the space does not mean sharing what sits in it.What goes away is a guaranteed slice. If one member backs up years of phone videos, the others could run short. Any extra storage the account holder buys also lands in the common pool.Microsoft calls the new model more flexible. Unused space no longer sits idle, and a heavy user is no longer stuck at 1TB while others have room to spare. That suits a household with one power user. A family of four using 500GB each, however, will have to buy more space to keep what they already have.New and upgraded subscriptions moved to shared storage on October 8. Existing Family and Premium subscribers will switch at their first renewal on or after May 2, 2027, and Microsoft says they will be notified in detail before that. Moving to another eligible plan earlier, say from Family to Premium, could bring the change forward.Some existing users in eligible markets may get transitional bonus storage at the switch. Microsoft has not said how much, or who qualifies.The storage cut comes bundled with a perk. Until now, only the primary account holder on a Family or Premium plan could use Copilot and the AI features inside Office apps. Over the coming months, those benefits will extend to up to five other members, with controls to manage AI access for younger users.Separate limits for individual AI features will also give way to a single usage allowance, with the option to buy more. Households that lean on Copilot heavily could end up paying extra.The reaction has been sharp. A widely upvoted Reddit post is urging subscribers to switch off auto-renewal and cite the storage cut in Microsoft's cancellation survey, and some users say they already have. The change also arrives as AI data centres absorb more of the world's storage supply, with hard drive prices up 46% between September 2025 and January 2026. Microsoft has not linked the decision to costs.Families now get AI for everyone and less room for their files. They have until next May to decide if that is worth renewing.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans drop from 6TB to a shared 2TB OneDrive pool. Existing Microsoft 365 subscribers get the new OneDrive limit after May 2, 2027. Copilot and AI features can now be shared with everyone on the plan.

Article Title: Anthropic’s answer to AI-powered hacking is more AI, offering free Mythos security scans to open-source developers
Article Text:
Anthropic’s fix for AI hacking: more AI

Anthropic’s OSS Scanner flagged just one false alarm in testing

Only critical open-source projects can sign up for the free AI scans

Anthropic is putting its most powerful AI models, including Claude Mythos, to work on the open-source code that much of the internet is built on. The company has introduced OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service that runs periodic AI security scans on eligible open-source projects and sends maintainers detailed vulnerability reports.The catch is that the reports are written entirely by AI. No human reviews or triages them before they reach a maintainer, and Anthropic admits some findings could be incorrect or invalid. Its argument is speed. With exploits now being built within minutes of a flaw surfacing, the company says projects that can find and fix bugs faster stand a better chance against attackers chasing the same weaknesses.Each report comes with a self-contained reproducer, an explanation of the bug, a bisection showing when it entered the code where possible, and a candidate patch when one is available. Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of projects. Its penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects, and 85 of them, or 88%, met the bar for its coordinated disclosure process. Of the other 12, 11 were real bugs already reported elsewhere, leaving a single false positive.Early testers back that up. wolfSSL said all but two of the 74 reports it received were valid, and five became CVEs.curl creator Daniel Stenberg said the scanner helped surface one of the worst curl vulnerabilities reported in the last few years.Enrolment is not open to every repository. Anthropic is borrowing its criteria from Google’s OSS-Fuzz, which has scanned open-source software with fuzzers since 2016, so only projects with a critical impact on infrastructure and user security will qualify, decided case by case. Core maintainers apply by submitting a pull request on GitHub. The service reportedly runs under Anthropic’s consumer terms, which allow inputs and outputs to be used for model training.OSS Scanner grows out of Project Glasswing. Over the past six months, Anthropic’s models flagged more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities in major software, but its team could manually verify only about 6,000. Language models now catch over 85% of vulnerabilities on the CyberGym benchmark, up from under 20% at the start of 2025.The stakes are familiar. Open-source projects are often run by unpaid volunteers, and the 2024 XZ Utils backdoor showed how a single compromised library could expose millions of systems. Anthropic expects attackers to keep the upper hand for the next two years, until AI catches bugs before they ship.
Article Summary: OSS Scanner runs periodic AI security scans on eligible open-source projects. No human reviews or triages them before they reach a maintainer, and Anthropic admits some findings could be incorrect or invalid. Anthropic spent several weeks testing the pipeline with dozens of projects. Its penetration testers checked 97 critical and high-severity findings across 48 projects.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella tells industry: Software is not going anywhere but ...
Article Text:
Satya Nadella

So much of what we do at work is still spent working around software. We switch between apps, rebuild context each time, and translate what we want to do into the steps each system expects. AI is changing that, helping us organize software around the work, rather than us working around the software.

We’ve already seen an early version of this shift in software development, one of the first areas to adopt agents at scale.

As agentic development has grown, GitHub has seen accelerating repo creation and PR and commit activity. The lesson is that more agents don’t make systems of record less important. They make trusted places to maintain information, coordinate changes, and manage state even more important. We see a similar pattern in sales, customer service, finance, and ops.

It’s why our ambition is to make Copilot a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task.

Merging the ‘head’ with the ‘headless’ layer

But a new front end like Copilot (the “head”) is only half the story. We also need a governed foundation that makes the underlying business logic and context historically locked inside individual CRM, ERP, and other apps available to agents (the “headless” layer).

After all, a model’s intelligence only becomes useful to a business when it has the right context and the right tools to act. You need a system that can understand someone’s intent, bring in the relevant organizational and business context, and invoke the right workflows.

For us, that means bringing together Copilot as the multi-model harness and agentic layer, the business logic in our apps, and the systems of record they run on, combined with connectors to other data sources.

Microsoft IQ connects those layers together.

This gives Copilot and agents a rich understanding of the business, connecting organizational knowledge with business data, processes and tools so they can reason over the work and act within the rules of the enterprise. It is not just about exposing existing APIs to an LLM, but architecting business context itself for AI.

It’s why today we announced 30+ new Copilot skills across Dynamics 365 Sales, Service and Customer Insights, as Jeff explains here, bringing these CRM capabilities directly into the flow of work.

And it’s just the start for us.

With these skills, you can use Copilot across Chat, Cowork, Autopilot, and even Code to complete even more end to end workflows across your business.

But it’s not just about getting work done with Copilot.

We’ve also introduced

Microsoft Copilot

Managed Runtime, which provides hosting infra which lets code run safely inside your company’s environment, governed by IT.

When you put it all together, you get something much more powerful than yet another AI feature inside SaaS. You start to get what I think of as an infinite SaaS factory.

Think about simply going to Code in Copilot, describing what your business needs, and building a customization or an entirely new Saas module.

With these plugins and skills, you can extend our Dataverse schema, build on existing business logic, and create new experiences and workflows connected to the systems your business already runs on.

We are entering a new era of truly “personal” software, where you can easily tailor the apps you use to the way you work, but stay connected to the systems of record your business already runs on, preventing fragmentation of your most important systems.

And the opportunity is bigger than simply extending the systems we have today. We can reinvent systems of record for an agentic world to handle high-volume agent access, bring together context and intelligence across data sources, and work natively with assistants like Copilot. For some customers, that will mean extending existing systems. For others, it will mean replacing them.

With Code and these underlying skills, you are doing all this with essentially zero friction, meaning it’s easy to quickly customize what you build and adapt from one project to another as your business changes.

And importantly this is not about using an LLM for everything. Because these skills are deeply integrated with your systems of record, we can use tokens where intelligence actually adds value, while relying on deterministic software for execution when that is faster, cheaper and more reliable.

I believe all this can reset business SaaS.

The opportunity is to reinvent systems of record for an agentic world, not just build new experiences on top of them, while giving every business an entirely new way to orchestrate work and build what is missing.

That is the direction we are taking at Microsoft: Copilot as a new OS for work, with a governed infinite SaaS factory built in.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has suggested that software is not going anywhere and once again, argued autonomous agents and generative tools are fundamentally reorganising how people interact with corporate technology, essentially helping people organise software around the work, rather than them working around the software. Speaking on the changing architecture of enterprise tools, Nadella explained in a post on X (formerly Twitter) that workers have spent decades having to “work around software”, wasting hours toggling between siloed applications, rebuilding lost context and translating tasks into rigid database commands.According to Nadella, artificial intelligence reverses that dynamic, organising software around actual tasks rather than forcing humans to adapt to fragmented tools. Nadella pointed to early trends in software engineering on GitHub as proof that agentic tools do not diminish traditional platforms. Despite autonomous coding agents completing large volumes of work, GitHub has experienced accelerating repository creation, along with higher pull-request and commit activity.Microsoft’s overarching ambition is to turn Copilot into a universal operating system for work that spans every underlying model, computing form factor, and daily assignment.Nadella emphasised that deploying an intuitive user interface – the “head” – is only half the equation. Enterprise agents require governed access to the “headless” layer where business logic and operational records reside inside CRM and ERP suites. Here’s how he explained this:
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced 30+ new Copilot skills across Dynamics 365 Sales, Service and Customer Insights. The skills are deeply integrated with your systems of record. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella believes this is the direction we are taking at Microsoft.

Article Title: Is the Apple iPhone 17 worth buying in this year’s festive season sales
Article Text:
The festive iPhone to buy

The festive discount on the iPhone 17 mostly undoes Apple’s price hike

A year on, the iPhone 17 has aged better than most base iPhones

The iPhone 17 still makes more sense than waiting or going older

Every festive sale, the iPhone that actually moves is last year's. The new model gets the spotlight and the billboards, while the outgoing one, suddenly a lot cheaper, quietly ends up in most shopping carts. It went that way with the iPhone 13 in 2022, the iPhone 14 a year later and the 15 and 16 after that, so it's no surprise to see the iPhone 17 headlining this week's festive sales.What's different this year is that the iPhone 17 has nothing to make way for. Apple unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo in September but held back the regular iPhone 18, which isn't expected before early 2027. For once, last year's iPhone is also the newest regular one on the shelf, and that makes it the festive pick more than it has ever been.The only catch is the price tag. The iPhone 17 went on sale in India in September 2025 at Rs 82,900 for 256GB, and once the iPhone 18 Pro arrived, Apple moved it up to Rs 99,900. The phone now costs Rs 17,000 more than it did on day one, so it pays to look closely at what this year's festive offers actually save.Take Flipkart's offer, the one most buyers will have come across this week. The 256GB iPhone 17 sells for Rs 84,999 during Big Billion Days, an ICICI Bank or Axis Bank credit card takes off another Rs 2,000, and trading in an old phone adds an exchange bonus of up to Rs 3,000 on top of its value.Stack all three and you arrive at the Rs 79,999 figure doing the rounds.Flipkart is only one of many, though, with iPhone 17 offers running across online platforms and retail stores this festive season, and a few examples show how varied they are. Reliance Digital has the phone at Rs 79,899 and bank and exchange offers that can bring it to around Rs 69,000. Retailer Unicorn, meanwhile, isn't waiting for a sale at all, putting the iPhone 17 at an effective Rs 78,900 in its stores once up to Rs 5,000 in instant cashback on Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and SBI Card credit cards and an exchange bonus of up to Rs 8,000 are counted, with no-cost EMI stretching to 24 months.Without the right credit card or an old phone to trade in, you're paying roughly what buyers paid last September. Most of the festive discount, in other words, is the hike being walked back.And the search doesn't have to stay online. Other retailers, and even the neighbourhood electronics store, often match these prices through the festive season, so they're worth a visit too.Wherever you end up buying it, paying close to last year's price still counts for plenty this year, with new phones arriving well above the ones they replace. The iPhone 18 Pro, for one, starts at Rs 1,64,900, a full Rs 30,000 more than the iPhone 17 Pro did, so for a current-generation iPhone, that is about as generous as things are likely to get for a while.It helps that the phone itself has worn its first year well. The iPhone 17 was the first regular iPhone in a long while to leave very little on the table for the Pro models, bringing a 120Hz ProMotion display with always-on after years of the base iPhone sitting at 60Hz while Android phones at half the price moved on. Storage doubled to 256GB, the ultrawide jumped from 12 to 48 megapixels, and an 18-megapixel square selfie sensor let Center Stage widen the frame as friends crowded in, without anyone turning the phone sideways.None of that feels dated a year later. The iPhone 17 has been my everyday phone through that entire stretch. The A19 hasn't lost its edge either, and still handles editing photos, bouncing between work chats and a dozen browser tabs, or even a long evening of gaming without a hiccup without a stutter, and everything on that 120Hz screen still feels as snappy as it did on day one.The battery, rated at up to 30 hours of video playback, still gets me comfortably through to bedtime with the always-on display switched on. The cameras have aged just as well, with the 48-megapixel pair still turning out sharp, natural-looking photos by day and dependable ones at night.The software has moved along as well. iOS 26 arrived with its share of grumbles, from a Liquid Glass design that made parts of the interface harder to read to Apple Intelligence feeling thin without the Siri overhaul people had been waiting for. iOS 27 has put much of its effort into smoothing those rough edges, and it finally brings that Siri along.That new Siri AI is the biggest change the iPhone 17 has seen since it went on sale. Siri can now hold a proper conversation, answer open-ended questions, read what's on screen and draw on messages and documents on the phone, while a new Camera mode can split a bill from a photo of the receipt. It works in English in India for now, with Hindi still to come.What it lacked last year, of course, it still lacks. There's no telephoto camera, so zooming past 2x means cropping. At 6.3 inches it is nowhere near the compact iPhones a loyal few still miss. If either was a dealbreaker in 2025, a discounted price tag won't change that now.If you’re still on the fence, it’s worth going back to what I made of the iPhone 17 when I first used it last year . Just keep the changes covered here in mind as you read it.Holding out usually pays off only when the next model promises a lot more for the same money, and this time the signs point to neither. The iPhone 18 is expected around March alongside the iPhone 18e, and the bigger changes, including a smaller Dynamic Island and new cameras, look set to stay with the Pro models. With prices where they're headed, expecting it to land at Rs 99,900, let alone below it, is wishful thinking too.Which is why the old festive rule of picking last year's iPhone has rarely been easier to follow. Anyone still on an iPhone 13, iPhone 14 or older, especially a 60Hz model whose battery has seen better days, will feel the jump the first time they scroll, and so will Android users who have wanted an iPhone without paying Pro prices. iPhone 16 owners are the ones who can sit this one out, since a smoother screen alone is a hard sell for another Rs 80,000.The iPhone 16 is also the obvious alternative on sale, going for somewhere between Rs 65,000 and Rs 72,000. It costs less today, but it does without the 120Hz screen and the upgraded cameras, which happen to be what will keep the 17 feeling current four or five years down the line. Step further back to the iPhone 15, which Flipkart has from Rs 63,999, and Siri AI goes off the table altogether.So yes, this year's festive discount is mostly a price correction. But last year's iPhone has been the smart festive buy for a while now, and with no new regular model sitting beside it, the iPhone 17 has never had an easier case to make. If you need an iPhone before March, this is the one to get.
Article Summary: The festive discount on the iPhone 17 mostly undoes Apple’s price hike. The iPhone 17 went on sale in India in September 2025 at Rs 82,900 for 256GB. Once the iPhone 18 Pro arrived, Apple moved it up to Rs 99,900. The phone now costs Rs 17,000 more than it did on day one.

Article Title: Google Cloud launches universal ‘Gemini Agent’ with deep app integration
Article Text:
How Google’s Gemini Agent operates

Unified Interface and API:

Omnipresent and headless deployment:

Deep context:

Deep integration across Google Workspace apps

Personal Assistance:

Google Cloud unveiled the Gemini agent at its annual Gemini at Work 2026 conference, positioning the system as a universal, single digital assistant engineered to handle enterprise knowledge work, run complex code and execute multi-step workflows straight from a prompt box. According to Google Cloud, nearly 500 enterprise customers each processed over one trillion tokens in the past year alone. Furthermore, approximately 80% of all Google Cloud clients now deploy its artificial intelligence offerings, while nearly 90% of Fortune 100 enterprises actively use Gemini Enterprise. With business environments pivoting toward agentic systems, Google stated that the new Gemini agent is built around delegating end objectives rather than micromanaging step-by-step instructions.The Gemini agent is designed around six core architectural pillars.Users can chat, delegate autonomous objectives, schedule background duties, and generate code from a consolidated interface without switching between disconnected applications.The system functions across web interfaces, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. It integrates directly into developer command lines, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack, or operates headlessly behind third-party enterprise tools.Running entirely on cloud infrastructure, the agent retains a shared memory bank and personalization graph across all endpoints. Users can initiate a job that runs for hours or days, close their computer, and return to completed deliverables without re-briefing the system.When handling complex projects, Gemini can spin up specialised, temporary sub-agents to tackle parallel or sequential tasks. It can also stand up permanent "coworker agents" assigned to specific team functions. These coworker agents receive their own dedicated email addresses (such as @agents.company.com), independent cloud storage, and role boundaries.The system retains four distinct layers of memory: session memory for active jobs; semantic memory for company documentation; procedural memory for repeatable workflows; and episodic memory to recall past interactions.Flexible multi-model routing: The agent decouples the user experience from the underlying foundation model. It dynamically routes queries to the most cost-effective and accurate engine available, navigating Google’s own Gemini family alongside Anthropic’s Claude models, with support for future private and open-source models.The agent works directly across Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, Sheets, Chat and Calendar through three primary modes:Knowing a user’s schedule and team relationships, the agent can coordinate across apps automatically. For example, it can assemble an attendee list from past chat threads, review calendars, and send scheduling emails without requiring manual contact entry.Built-in Workspace Intelligence identifies tasks within inbound emails, such as a manager requesting a presentation, and serves up one-click prompts allowing users to delegate the task directly to Gemini. The inbox also highlights messages based on operational importance rather than arrival time.Departments can generate artificial colleagues that show up directly in corporate directories with their own calendar and Drive storage. Team members can tag the coworker agent in Chat or add them to document comments, where the agent suggests edits and answers questions under its own identity without exposing wider personal files.
Article Summary: The Gemini agent is designed around six core architectural pillars. Users can chat, delegate autonomous objectives, schedule background duties, and generate code from a consolidated interface. The system functions across web interfaces, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. It integrates directly into developer command lines, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack.

Article Title: Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes: Ice Caves Biome, Frostbite Mob, and more
Article Text:
Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 is out with new features from the upcoming game drop (Image via Mojang)

Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes

New Features

Added the new Ice Caves Biome

Added Ice Crystals

Added Icicles

Added the Frostbite mob

Added the Freezing mob effect

Added the Ice Ball

Ice Caves

The Ice Cave is a new cave biome that generates beneath colder Overworld biomes.

It's built mainly from Packed Ice and Calcite, with Icicles hanging from the ceiling and Large Icicles made of Packed Ice forming both on the ground and overhead.

Patches of Snow occasionally appear on the floor, and ores generate embedded within pockets of Stone and Deepslate.

Alongside typical cave mobs, Strays and Frostbites can also spawn in this biome, and Ice Crystals occasionally generate on the ground.

Ice Crystal is a new crystal-like block similar to Amethyst Clusters. It breaks if its support block is removed, emits light, and can be placed in any direction.

Icicle is a new block in the same family as Dripstone and Sulfur Spikes. Icicles can naturally grow up to 5 blocks long when pointing downward, but only in areas without nearby light sources and never in the Nether.

Frostbite

The Frostbite is a new zombie variant capable of throwing Ice Balls.

It spawns in cold and icy biomes and switches between melee and ranged combat depending on target distance and whether it's currently holding Ice Balls.

Melee attacks apply the Freezing effect, while ranged attacks throw Ice Balls directly.

Frostbites transform into regular Zombies if left underwater long enough, and they drop Rotten Flesh and Ice Balls on death.

They can stand on top of Powder Snow and are immune to freezing, so neither the Freezing effect nor Powder Snow slows them down.

Interestingly, regular Zombies and Husks will transform into Frostbites if they stand inside Powder Snow.

Freezing Mob Effect

The Freezing effect causes affected players to shake and eventually take damage, gradually freezing them as though standing in Powder Snow for the duration.

Leather Armor offers protection from freezing, the same way it does against Powder Snow, though it won't prevent the effect from being applied or remove it once active.

Mobs vulnerable to Freezing take a 5x damage multiplier while affected.

Lingering Potions, Splash Potions, and a new Potion of Freezing can all be brewed using Ice Balls, and Arrows of Freezing can be crafted by placing a Lingering Potion of Freezing in the center of a crafting table surrounded by eight Arrows.

Ice Ball

Ice Balls are the new projectile thrown by Frostbites. They deal a small amount of damage along with knockback, dealing up to 4 damage on impact, scaling down based on velocity. They break apart on contact with blocks or entities, triggering a particle effect and sound.

Changes

Minor tweaks to Blocks, Items and Entities

Snow can now be placed on Packed Ice

Snowballs now apply knockback to players

UI

Lightmap visualization is now configurable as lightmap_texture in debug options and appears in the Light group; its visibility is saved with the debug profile and can now be displayed alongside the FPS and network charts

The Social Interactions screen has been replaced with the new Other Players screen

The "Social Interactions" keybind has been renamed to "Other Players"

The Friends button has received a new icon

The "Visibility" option has moved from Online Options into the Friends list

Icon buttons in the pause menu have been reordered to match the main menu

Friends

Updated the design of the Friends list

Added searching - the profile name text box in the Friends tab now doubles as a search box, and a search box appears in the requests tab once you have 15 or more pending requests

Added sorting - a new sort button cycles between sorting by who's online and alphabetical order

Clicking a player's icon in the Friends list now opens their Player Options

Removed the "Remove Friend" button; this is now handled through Player Options instead

Player Reporting

Redesigned the save/discard draft confirmation screen

Saved report drafts no longer prompt you to discard them when exiting a world, if they can be continued later

Chat reports can never be continued; Name and Skin reports can be continued if the reported player is still in your Friends list

Pressing "Quit Game" in the main menu now warns you if an unsent draft report would be lost

Debug Overlay

Added chunk_section_status, showing the rendering status of chunks around you (impacts performance at high view distances)

Split the chunk load overlay off from visualize_chunks_on_server into a new chunk_load_status

Technical Changes

Data Pack version is now 123.0

Resource Pack version is now 100.0

Numerous world generation changes, including a reworked minecraft:speleothem_cluster feature with new placement options, a renamed minecraft:large_dripstone feature, new Ice Cave ore placements, a new minecraft:block_sound_set registry, several new block/item/biome tags for pathfinding and ore replacement, and a new minecraft:freezing particle type

Numerous new block, item, UI, and entity textures and sounds added to support Ice Caves, Icicles, Ice Crystals, the Frostbite, and the Freezing effect

Several UI textures renamed or removed as part of the Friends and Other Players redesign

Fixed Bugs in 26.4 Snapshot 3

MC-212616 - The dye staining sound does not play when dyes are used on tamed wolves or cats

MC-303468 - Pets can be teleported to incorrect coordinates when going through a nether portal

MC-306017 - The main arm doesn't swing when making a tamed wolf sit or stand while holding a matching dye

MC-307830 - Framerate limited to 20 fps with the Vulkan rendering backend on some systems

MC-308037 - Unselected tabs in the friends menu show white text instead of gray

MC-308051 - Icons on several buttons don't adhere to the UI pixel grid

MC-308747 - The social interactions button is grayed out in LAN worlds with no players

MC-308994 - The Chat Restrictions screen doesn't display Xbox communication settings affecting chat

MC-309896 - Missing periods on two tooltip strings

MC-309906 - Inconsistent capitalization of "Friends List" across strings

MC-310124 - Leaving a keyboard-opened menu doesn't reselect its button on the previous screen

MC-310237 - A friends error string uses an em dash inconsistently

MC-310854 - Inconsistent button outlines in the friends screen

MC-311932 - Caps Lock could no longer trigger sprint/sneak toggles set to "Hold"

MC-311963 - A Poplar leaves subtitle string used incorrect grammar

MC-312120 - Exclusive Fullscreen toggle button doesn't update properly in windowed mode

MC-312198 - Almost no small mushrooms generate on mushroom islands

MC-312213 - Game crashes with custom Superflat presets containing air

Article Title: Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 cross platform? Crossplay and multiplayer explained
Article Text:
Minecraft Dungeons II officially supports cross-platform (Image via Mojang)

Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 crossplay?

How co-op works in Minecraft Dungeons II

Turning on Cross-platform in Minecraft Dungeons II

Launch Minecraft Dungeons II and go to the main menu.

Open Settings and look for the Game options section.

Find Cross-Platform Play and toggle it on.

Crossplay vs. Cross-Progression

Subscription requirements

Minecraft Dungeons II launched on September 29, 2026, and the new dungeon crawler has received a solid reception from the community. For anyone planning to squad up with friends across different consoles, the good news arrived early: crossplay is fully supported.If you are looking for further details, you are at the right place. Here's a breakdown of how multiplayer works, what crossplay actually covers, and what to know before jumping into a session.Yes. Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform play across every system it launched on: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, for parties of up to four players. This builds on a feature the original Minecraft Dungeons already had, so Mojang carried the functionality forward into the sequel rather than building it from scratch.Official store listings and Xbox have both confirmed cross-platform multiplayer and cross-platform co-op, meaning a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Mojang hasn't published a detailed platform-by-platform compatibility chart, so the exact mechanics of every possible pairing aren't fully spelled out.Minecraft Dungeons II supports up to four players at once, whether that's entirely online, entirely local couch co-op, or a mix of both happening in the same session.That hybrid option, officially called Mixed Co-Op, is one of the sequel's standout multiplayer additions, since the original game required players to choose one mode or the other rather than blending them.Joining a session works two ways: through matchmaking, which fills empty slots automatically, or by sharing an eight-character party code with friends so they can join a specific lobby directly, regardless of what platform they're on.Cross-platform play is tied to account sign-in rather than being fully automatic. To enable it:Once enabled, the setting stays active going forward unless manually turned off from the same menu.It's worth separating two related but different features. Crossplay lets players on different platforms share a session together. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another. Mojang has confirmed that hero data is stored online rather than locally, so progress follows players who sign in with the same Microsoft account across devices.Online console multiplayer isn't entirely free of extra requirements. Xbox players need an active Game Pass tier that includes online multiplayer, while PlayStation players need an active PlayStation Plus subscription to play online. PC players don't need anything beyond owning the game, and it's also available through Game Pass on day one as an Xbox Play Anywhere title.To conclude it all, squads spread across different consoles can enjoy Minecraft Dungeons II together. Now you can easily jump into a friend's game using party codes and have a blast playing the game. The big things to double check before you go are having an active online subscription on consoles and making sure cross platform play is toggled on in settings.
Article Summary: Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform multiplayer and co-op. This means a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another.

Its design includes a low roof, a long bonnet, a short front overhang and large 23-inch wheels. The car also has a 50:50 weight distribution, which is aimed at improving handling.Jaguar has also added intelligent torque vectoring and active aerodynamics to improve performance. These features include movable air vents and a rear spoiler that can extend in three stages. The car has a drag coefficient of 0.23, helping it move through the air more efficiently.The Type 01 has a cabin designed around luxury and technology. A central section divides the interior into four separate areas.The cabin features brass-effect aluminium trim, a 24-inch OLED driver display made from a single piece of glass and a separate 7-inch touchscreen. It also gets a full-width panoramic soundbar and seats with audio features designed to improve the listening experience.Jaguar says the name Type 01 reflects both its history and its future. The word "Type" pays tribute to famous models from the brand's past. The number "0" represents zero emissions, while "1" marks the first car of its new generation.The car also benefits from technology developed through Jaguar TCS Racing's Formula E programme, which has won two world championships.The Type 01 can accelerate from 62 mph to 112 mph (100km/h to 180km/h) in just 4.0 seconds.Designed, engineered and manufactured in the UK, the Type 01 is an important part of Jaguar's move towards becoming a fully electric luxury car brand. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500. Higher-specification versions and customised models are expected to cost more than £150,000.Jaguar plans to open order books in early 2027, with the first customer deliveries expected in the second half of the year.Also read: Sebastien Buemi ends full-time Formula E career, stays with Envision as advisor
Article Summary: The Type 01 is Jaguar's new flagship electric car. It has three electric motors that produce 1,030PS of power and 1,365Nm of torque. It can go from 0 to 62 mph in just 3.2 seconds. Prices start at £130,000, with the US price listed at $130,500.

Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal
Article Text:
Formula E and Comsol

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development. It will introduce what Formula E describes as its fastest and most technologically advanced race car so far.COMSOL has also announced COMSOL Multiphysics version 2027, which is scheduled to arrive later this autumn.The new version will include features aimed at advanced engineering work, including dedicated electric motor modelling, system-level simulation, agentic modelling and wider access to tools for creating simulation apps.The partnership was announced at the COMSOL Conference 2026 Boston. Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier also delivered a keynote speech at the event, discussing the technology and engineering that could shape the future of Formula E.
Article Summary: Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology. Aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process. AI and digital twins also in focus as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.

Article Title: From crash-test airbags to Formula E: Heron Preston’s journey with discarded materials
Article Text:
Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion

From sanitation uniforms to Formula E: Heron Preston gives waste a new life

Heron Preston brings crash-test airbags, recycled materials into Formula E fashion

From fashion to motorsport for Heron Preston

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Heron Preston, discarded materials are not simply waste. They can become something new. The designer has built his work around finding new uses for materials that are often overlooked. Now, that approach is coming to motorsport through a creative partnership with Formula E, where fashion, performance and sustainability will come together. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport.Heron Preston has explored the potential of unwanted materials through several projects. His 2016 UNIFORM project used upcycled decommissioned New York City Department of Sanitation uniforms and second-hand garments.More recently, he worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments. The clothes retained the distinctive physical qualities of the material. His approach is based on looking closely at every part of a product, from the materials used to how they are made and the people and processes involved. He calls this concept eX-Ray.ID@undefined Caption not available.Rather than simply choosing existing fabrics, eX-Ray looks at how materials can be developed and used in a more considered way.For the Formula E partnership, Heron Preston is using recycled cotton made from pre-consumer factory off-cuts and production scraps. The materials are sorted, shredded and re-spun into new yarn before being developed into a heavyweight, tightly woven fabric. The idea fits with Formula E’s own focus on recovering and reusing resources.While Preston turns recovered materials into new designs, Formula E uses regenerative braking to recover energy and use it again for racing. Together, the two sides want to explore how this thinking can be applied to motorsport fashion from the beginning of the design process.The partnership will look at more than clothing. The partners hope to explore performance wear, fan merchandise, accessories and products made from upcycled materials drawn from the sport. They also want to find new uses for components and materials after their life in racing.The GEN4 car provides an example of Formula E’s approach. It is designed to be 100% recyclable or reusable, with at least 20% recycled materials across key components.Talking about the same, Heron Preston said, “This creative partnership is about rethinking what motorsport fashion can be. I’ve always been interested in taking materials, processes and ideas from unexpected places and finding new ways to give them purpose. Working with Formula E gives me the opportunity to bring that approach into a world where performance is everything. We’re looking at how apparel can be thoughtfully designed from the material up, balancing function, quality and a more considered approach to how things are made.The partnership will be previewed at ComplexCon Los Angeles on October 3 and 4. The event will feature an exploration of eX-Ray materials and a GEN4 Formula E car with an exclusive Preston-designed livery.Ellie Norman, Chief Marketing Officer, Formula E, said, “Heron and Formula E share a curiosity about how things work and how they can be made better. In racing, we push for greater performance while using energy and materials more efficiently. Heron brings a complementary perspective, exploring what existing materials can become through design. This partnership gives us the opportunity to develop those ideas together and apply them to the products people wear. ComplexCon is the first look at that shared ambition, with the potential to build a more considered approach to motorsport fashion over time.”Also read: Formula E, Heron Preston join hands to bring recycled materials to motorsport fashion
Article Summary: Designer Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport. Preston has previously worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments.
